title: Andy’s back to the gym, PPL
desc:
I’m getting back into the gym after a decent time off, wanting to take advantage of all the gains I can get (leaving nothing on the table). This push pull legs programme is pretty basic but hits all areas it needs to and is easily scalable. 

Everything is broken down to 3-4 sets per exercise and each set will include somewhere between 8 and 15 reps. Take advantage of this and push it hard, 1 or two reps before failure, if you don’t feel that then increase the weight. This makes it easy to keep track of the progress and to take full advantage of progressive overload. 

The rep range is there so that if you get to the upper end and still have some gas in the tank then increase the load to the point that the lower end of the Teo range is getting much harder to complete, once that weight is in the upper end then increase it yet again. Enjoy!!

ex.note: 45 degree bench, try to get the dumbbells to touch your outer perch at the lowered position. Nice and slow on the eccentric movement and try to pause for a short moment at the bottom of the rep

Flat bench press. You’ll see a theme here, slow on the way down, nice little pause and explode up. RPE is set to 8 based on there not being a spotter. If you have a spotter, increase that and go heavy
Keep this one a little lighter for more reps. You’ll feel the burn. If you don’t have access to a pec deck machine, hit some normal fly’s
Warm up with an empty bar and gradually build the weight up if you haven’t done this before. If the strict press gets hard, give it a little leg drive on the way up and control it on the way down
Don’t need all that much weight to get some high RPE with 15 reps. Keep the shoulders safe and research the correct form
Alternatively use the same movement but with dumbbells, cable gives better tension throughout the whole rep range. Start light and move heavier when you’re comfortable with the movement
Final exercise now so make it count and get that lovely horseshoe Tricep look. Final set push all the way to failure
Wide grip
Can be done with barbell, kettle bells, cables or anything else. Dumbbell is my preference for freedom of movement. Go heavy on this
No pec deck, no problem. Just get yourself on a high bench and use dumbbells or if you have cables then rear flys will also work just fine
If you’re reaching 12 reps you need to increase the weight, we all know that biceps are the most important one
Wait until you’ve recovered from the hammer curls before you start this. You’ll thank me later when you have the pump of your lifetime. Go to failure on all 3 sets. If you aren’t, increase the weight
One of the best compound movements out there. This is week 1 and form is super important here so keep the squats light today, you can increase the weight once your form is consistent and strong
If you have somewhat flexible hamstrings, elevate your feet increase the stretch. Focus on time under tension, try not to let the plates quite touch the ground, keep the movement at the hips
Don’t ego lift but do keep it heavy

I know you don’t want to, but you have to, your calves are tiny. 

If you find yourself struggling with stability and balance, put some weight in a back pack and support yourself using a wall or bar
3 sets to failure, allow a good time to recover between sets. Remember these are crunches, not sit ups. Think of keeping your Lowe back set in place and rounding the shoulders to lift the chest
If these are too hard, try bending your legs and pulling your knees to your chest, alternatively lie on your back and do leg raises like that. Again, 3 sets to complete failure
If you have a spot, use them. If you have a smith machine, use that and you can increase the weight
Start with a weight you’re confident in and then the final 2 sets you want to push yourself close to failure
Here’s your pump for the day
Bring your elbows in a tad and really open your chest up to the sky
Another super pumpy one. Keep the load a little lighter and get all of those precious reps in
Push the weight up again here. Use a rope to get a nice squeeze at the end or a straight bar to keep the weight up a tad
I’d suggest using an EZ bar here as it’s much easier to scale the weight properly and reduce rust of any injury. Keep the arms back 45 degrees and allow yourself to feel a deep stretch at the bottom
This can become quite fatiguing on the grip so I would warm up properly, start heavy and do a drop set
No worries if you don’t have a row machine, I don’t. Just move the cable to the lowest position and sit straight legged on the floor with your feet against the cable machine
One of the best feeling in the world. Make sure to get the form right otherwise you won’t be focusing the load where it wants to be
Start position of the rep wants to have the cable coming off your hand at a right angle for maximum tension in the stretched position
